title: Plan AE: AI Comic & Webtoon
summary: Script → panels → image generation → character consistency → dialogue bubbles → publish
scenario: For creators building a serialized comic or webtoon, from script to publishable art.

steps.title: Script
steps.detail: Write the episode script with beats for setup, development and resolution, and what each panel must communicate. Webtoons pace for vertical mobile screens — one information beat per screen.
steps.tips: Lock the cliffhanger ending of each episode before writing, or serialization loses readers.

steps.title: Panel breakdown & storyboard
steps.detail: Turn the script into a shot list: panel count, shot size (close-up/wide), camera angle, expression and dialogue. Vertical webtoons usually run 8-15 panels; comic pages hold 4-6 panels.
steps.tips: One idea per panel — overloading a panel is the classic beginner mistake.

steps.title: Image generation
steps.detail: Generate panels in batch with a consistent style prompt (same series and keywords). Leonardo's Flux models and character references work well for turning comic line art into color.
steps.tips: Keep one style template and change only scene, action and camera per panel.

steps.title: Character consistency
steps.detail: Build a character reference sheet (front/side/full body/expressions) and use --cref or image-to-image feedback so characters don't warp across panels. Make 4-6 reference images for key characters and hand-pick the most faithful result per panel.
steps.tips: Test the consistency flow with one protagonist over three panels before rolling out a whole episode.

steps.title: Dialogue bubbles
steps.detail: Overlay bubbles, position dialogue, font size and balloon placement so reading order stays clear. Keep webtoon dialogue light — no more than two lines per screen.
steps.tips: Keep the balloon style uniform; read the dialogue aloud and cut anything clunky.

steps.title: Publish
steps.detail: Export long images or pages sized for the platform (webtoons commonly 1080×1920 slices), add a cover and a first-episode teaser. Update the series and mine reader comments for the next episode.
steps.tips: Bank three episodes before announcing a schedule so you never miss an update.

pitfalls.title: Characters warping per panel
pitfalls.detail: Consistency is the hardest part of comics; use reference sheets plus human picking, don't expect one-shot perfection.

pitfalls.title: Overloaded panels
pitfalls.detail: Cramming too much into one panel confuses readers; one idea per panel, control pacing with panel count.

pitfalls.title: Bloated dialogue
pitfalls.detail: AI loves verbose lines; keep dialogue under ~20 characters and skip anything the art already shows.

pitfalls.title: Style drift
pitfalls.detail: Include the style keywords in every prompt and reinforce with image-to-image feedback.
